description: Blue detectives are taking on global cases, as Sara and Hamza delve into Earth's most enigmatic and mysterious phenomena to track down clues and uncover answers regarding its strangest changes and evolutions. Stay alert and attentive as the SAR-locks solve the Case of 4 billion years.
summary: UnrolledAtlas turns a plain-language question about the Earth ("has Morocco been getting drier since the 90s?") into an explicit, editable analysis spec, then answers it with deterministic trend statistics on NASA POWER data (MERRA-2 reanalysis and GPM IMERG precipitation). The language model only drafts the spec; every number comes from code: monthly anomalies, OLS with an effective-sample-size t-test, Mann-Kendall with Sen's slope, the Hamed-Rao autocorrelation correction and a Pettitt change-point test. The app shows the naive and corrected p-values side by side, so students see why the method matters, and reports "unstable" when a series has no single trend.
details:
UnrolledAtlas turns a plain-language question about the Earth ("has Morocco been getting drier since the 90s?") into an explicit, editable analysis spec, then answers it with deterministic trend statistics on NASA POWER data (MERRA-2 reanalysis and GPM IMERG precipitation). The language model only drafts the spec; every number comes from code: monthly anomalies, OLS with an effective-sample-size t-test, Mann-Kendall with Sen's slope, the Hamed-Rao autocorrelation correction and a Pettitt change-point test. The app shows the naive and corrected p-values side by side, so students see why the method matters, and reports "unstable" when a series has no single trend.

> How it addresses the challenge

- Picks Earth variables from 128 NASA POWER monthly parameters, for any point or bounding box since 1981.

- Builds the time series, removes the seasonal cycle, tests the trend with both a parametric and a non-parametric method, with confidence intervals and p-values.

- Visualizes raw and anomaly series, fits, confidence band and change-point; explains the verdict in plain language with the variable's definition.

- Five built-in detective cases, one per kind of verdict: Arctic warming (up), Arctic sea ice (down), Maghreb rain and soil (no trend in the box mean), Sahel and Congo rain and Weddell sea ice (unstable, with change-points).
dataRefs: NASA POWER monthly API (community AG): MERRA-2 (GMAO) 2 m temperature, corrected precipitation, root-zone soil wetness, sea-ice fraction; GPM IMERG precipitation
projectRefs: Mann 1945; Kendall 1975; Sen 1968; Hamed & Rao 1998; Pettitt 1979; pymannkendall (test oracle).

Python, FastAPI, numpy/scipy, Rust + PyO3, React + Vite + ECharts, MongoDB Atlas, Arize Phoenix, llama.cpp (PrismML fork) with Ternary Bonsai 2 9B for local tests, Google Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite in production, Kamal 2 on Hetzner.
